title: Platelet Count Emergencies: Bleeding Context and Smear Review
subject: Hematology & ABG
preview: A low platelet count may reflect reduced production, increased destruction or sequestration; bleeding risk varies by cause and context.
quickRevision: A low platelet count may reflect reduced production, increased destruction or sequestration; bleeding risk varies by cause and context.
Look for bleeding, fever, neurologic symptoms, hemolysis and thrombosis before deciding on urgency.
Transfusion decisions are situation-specific; suspected thrombotic microangiopathy needs urgent etiologic evaluation.

sections.title: Interpret the result in context
points: A low platelet count may reflect reduced production, increased destruction or sequestration; bleeding risk varies by cause and context.
Confirm unexpected results with a smear to exclude platelet clumping and pseudothrombocytopenia.

sections.title: Clinical interpretation & next steps
points: Look for bleeding, fever, neurologic symptoms, hemolysis and thrombosis before deciding on urgency.
Transfusion decisions are situation-specific; suspected thrombotic microangiopathy needs urgent etiologic evaluation.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not treat an isolated automated count as definitive without considering the smear and clinical situation.

quiz.question: What should be checked when the platelet count is unexpectedly low?
options: Serum lipase as the only test
quiz.explanation: Peripheral smear for platelet clumping. Confirm unexpected results with a smear to exclude platelet clumping and pseudothrombocytopenia.
